label: DEEP-RESEARCH TASK: the CRUX — SOCIAL + MEDIA app embed feasibility in 2026. For EACH of:

findings.summary: Brutal honest verdict for a 2026 signage "Apps" library: the era of "paste a social URL and get a live wall" is over for the big social networks. Pure video platforms (YouTube, Vimeo, Twitch) are still clean official iframes and are S-effort, low-risk reuses of our STREAMING widget. But Instagram and Facebook KILLED frictionless public embeds — Instagram Basic Display API was permanently shut down Dec 4 2024 and Meta removed the legacy oEmbed endpoints in April 2025; both now require a reviewed Meta Developer app + access token, a Business/Creator account, and only let you pull authorized accounts (no arbitrary-user or hashtag-search feeds). X/Twitter retired its read API tiers in Feb 2026 (pay-per-use only); the free publish.x.com single-post embed still works but profile timelines are unreliable and hashtag feeds are gone. LinkedIn has no official feed embed at all. The reviews trio (Google, Yelp, Tripadvisor) have no clean official multi-review embed — they're API-key + attribution plays. Because of all this, every serious signage vendor (OptiSigns, Yodeck, ScreenCloud) does one of two things: (a) make the operator OAuth-log-in their OWN Business account, or (b) resell a PAID 3rd-party social-wall aggregator (Walls.io, EmbedSocial, Curator.io, Taggbox, Juicer, Flockler) at ~$19–$250/mo. The pleasant surprises: TikTok oEmbed is public/keyless (but single-video only), and Snapchat, Pinterest, Bluesky, and Threads all ship working official embeds (Threads needs a Meta token). Recommended posture: ship the easy video/embed apps now riding STREAMING/WEBPAGE, gate the hard social walls behind an aggregator integration (single API key the operator pastes, or a VenueOS-managed aggregator account billed as a line item), and be honest in the picker about which apps need a business-account login.

apps.name: YouTube
apps.howEmbedded2026: Fully official and stable. Standard youtube.com/embed iframe + IFrame Player API. Single video, playlist (videoseries?list=), channel-latest (via uploads playlist), and YouTube Live all embed unattended. Autoplay REQUIRES mute=1 (Chrome/Safari/Firefox block unmuted autoplay) and on locked-down kiosks may need the autoplay-policy flag. No API key needed for plain iframe; Data API key only if you want to resolve 'latest video on this channel' dynamically. No takedown risk.
apps.notes: We already do this in STREAMING. App layer = a YouTube-branded config form (paste channel/playlist/video/live URL, pick loop/mute/controls). The one gotcha is Taurus Chromium-83 autoplay + our inset-0 rule on any overlay chrome.

apps.name: Vimeo
apps.howEmbedded2026: Fully official and stable. player.vimeo.com iframe + Vimeo Player.js SDK. Add muted=1&autoplay=1&loop=1&autopause=0 for signage. Some accounts gate domain-level embed privacy (Pro/Business 'Where can this be embedded' allowlist) — operator may need to whitelist our player domain. No key for basic iframe.
apps.notes: Same path as YouTube. Surface the muted/loop/autopause defaults so signage 'just works'. Warn operators about the per-account embed-domain allowlist if their video is private.

apps.name: Twitch
apps.howEmbedded2026: Official iframe embed still works (live channel, VOD, clips) but has a HARD requirement: every embed must pass parent=<your-domain> (JS array if multiple), and the embedding domain MUST be HTTPS. On signage this means our player domain must be passed as the parent — a sandboxed null-origin iframe will fail the parent check, so a Twitch app needs a same-origin or proxied host, not our EXTERNAL_HTML null-origin sandbox.
apps.notes: The parent-domain + HTTPS + non-null-origin constraint is the real work — must mount in a WEBPAGE/STREAMING iframe that carries our actual origin, not the sandboxed EXTERNAL_HTML board. Set parent to the deployed player host.

apps.name: TikTok
apps.howEmbedded2026: Two very different paths. (1) oEmbed (https://www.tiktok.com/oembed?url=...) is PUBLIC, keyless — but returns markup for a SINGLE video only, not an account feed. Good for 'pin one TikTok'. (2) An auto-updating account feed needs the official Display API (OAuth login by the account owner) OR a paid aggregator. There is NO keyless way to show 'this account's latest videos' unattended.
apps.notes: Ship the single-video case first (keyless oEmbed → render returned HTML in a WEBPAGE iframe; loads tiktok's embed.js). For a rotating account wall, route to the aggregator path. oEmbed embed script needs network + same-origin-ish iframe, not our null-origin sandbox.

apps.name: Instagram
apps.howEmbedded2026: Public embeds are DEAD. Basic Display API permanently shut down Dec 4 2024; legacy oEmbed endpoints removed April 2025. In 2026 ANY Instagram feed needs: a Business or Creator account (personal accounts have zero API access), a registered Meta Developer app, an access token, AND Meta App Review/Advanced Access for oEmbed Read or Graph API. You can only display accounts the user authorizes — no arbitrary-user feeds, and hashtag/UGC discovery is heavily gated (≤30 hashtags/week, no Stories). This is why every signage vendor makes the operator 'Log in with Instagram (Business)'.
apps.notes: THE hard one. Realistic options: (a) operator OAuths their own Business/Creator account through OUR Meta app (requires us to pass Meta App Review for Instagram Graph + oEmbed Read — weeks of process), or (b) resell an aggregator (Walls.io/EmbedSocial/Curator) and just embed the aggregator's URL via WEBPAGE. Single-post oEmbed also needs our reviewed app token now. Do NOT promise 'paste any IG URL'.

apps.name: Facebook
apps.howEmbedded2026: Mixed. The Page Plugin (developers.facebook.com/docs/plugins/page-plugin) iframe STILL renders a public Page's timeline/posts without a token and is the cheapest path — but it's fragile, Meta-throttled, login-walled in some regions, and visually dated. The richer oEmbed Read for individual posts now requires a reviewed Meta app + token (legacy oEmbed removed April 2025). A clean curated wall = aggregator. Yodeck refreshes FB only every 10 min due to Meta rate limits.
apps.notes: Quick win = Page Plugin iframe in a WEBPAGE widget (public page only, no token) — but flag it as 'basic, may be throttled'. Anything beyond a raw page timeline (single posts, mixed wall) needs the reviewed-app token or an aggregator. Page Plugin needs a real origin, not null-sandbox.

apps.name: X / Twitter
apps.howEmbedded2026: publish.x.com still generates a FREE single-post (tweet) embed and a profile-timeline widget that loads via platform.twitter.com/widgets.js — single posts are reliable, profile timelines are increasingly flaky/broken, and hashtag timelines are no longer supported. The read API tiers (Basic/Pro) were retired Feb 2026 in favor of pay-per-use credits, so any API-backed wall now costs money. Most vendors push X behind a paid aggregator (EmbedSocial gates X to Premium+).
apps.notes: Ship single-post embed (free, via widgets.js in a WEBPAGE iframe) as the safe default. Offer profile timeline as 'beta / may break'. A reliable multi-source X wall = aggregator only. widgets.js needs network + non-null-origin frame.

apps.name: LinkedIn
apps.howEmbedded2026: NO official feed embed exists. LinkedIn killed company-page plugins and share badges years ago and never replaced them. Individual public posts have a native 'Embed this post' iframe (single post only). A live company-page feed is ONLY possible via a paid aggregator (Walls.io, EmbedSocial, Taggbox, SociableKit) — there is no keyless or first-party path.
apps.notes: Single-post embed = easy (paste the post's official embed iframe into WEBPAGE). Company feed = aggregator-only; treat as an aggregator-backed app, not a native one. Good B2B/CORPORATE-vertical differentiator if we resell an aggregator.

apps.name: Pinterest
apps.howEmbedded2026: OFFICIAL and working. Pinterest's own widget builder (Pin / Board / Profile widgets via pinit.js) is free, keyless, copy-paste, and renders a board of up to 50 pins unattended. Limited styling/moderation, but it works without OAuth or a business account.
apps.notes: Easy win and a rarity in 2026 — a real keyless official social embed. App = paste board/profile URL → we emit the official widget markup in a WEBPAGE iframe (needs pinit.js + real origin). Good for RETAIL/FASHION/HOSPITALITY verticals.

apps.name: Snapchat
apps.howEmbedded2026: OFFICIAL embeds exist (since 2023): Spotlight videos, Public Stories, Public Profiles, and Lenses each have a copy-paste embed code from the web Share menu. Keyless. Vertical/portrait format suits portrait signage. Caveat: only PUBLIC content, and it's single-item embeds, not a curated multi-source wall.
apps.notes: Niche but real. Most useful for youth/college/event signage. Paste embed code → WEBPAGE. Low priority vs IG/FB/X but genuinely low-friction since it's keyless. Confirm embed script parses in WebKit + Chromium-83 if it ever ships to a Taurus player.

apps.name: Threads
apps.howEmbedded2026: Official Threads oEmbed exists (developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/.../embed-a-threads-post) — BUT it's part of Meta oEmbed Read, so it requires a registered Meta app + access token (same machinery as IG/FB). Public posts only. There's also an in-app per-post embed snippet for single posts. No keyless account-feed path.
apps.notes: If we already stand up a Meta app for Instagram, Threads oEmbed rides the same token for nearly free. Single-post in-app embed is the keyless quick path. Bundle Threads into the same 'Meta apps' OAuth/token setup as IG/FB.

apps.name: Bluesky
apps.howEmbedded2026: OFFICIAL and keyless. Public oEmbed endpoint (https://embed.bsky.app/oembed) + per-post embed snippet; Bluesky is a registered oEmbed provider in oembed.com/providers.json. The embed JS re-fetches the post via API and renders media/quotes. Single-post today; account feeds via 3rd-party widgets (CommonNinja, SociableKit).
apps.notes: Cleanest modern social embed available — keyless oEmbed, open protocol, low takedown risk. Easy single-post app. Account-feed wall is 3rd-party for now. Nice 'we're current' signal even if low traffic.

apps.name: Google Business Profile / Reviews
apps.howEmbedded2026: NO official review-embed widget. Google offers only a Maps embed (shows the map, not a review wall) and the Places API (free but capped at ~5 reviews/location, requires an API key). A real review wall = a 3rd-party widget (Common Ninja, Shapo, Taggbox, Elfsight) that wraps the Places API, OR an aggregator. Attribution to Google required.
apps.notes: Highly demanded across RESTAURANT/RETAIL/HOSPITALITY/HEALTHCARE. Two builds: (a) we hold a Google Places API key, operator pastes their Place ID → we render a branded review card (caps at ~5 reviews, watch quota/billing), or (b) embed a 3rd-party widget URL. The native-key path is a strong differentiator since it's the most-asked-for review source.

apps.name: Yelp Reviews
apps.howEmbedded2026: No clean official embed. Yelp Fusion API returns up to 3 review EXCERPTS/business (free tier) or up to 7 (Pro Premium, paid), requires an API key, and mandates Yelp attribution + compliance with Fusion Terms. Native Yelp 'badge' embeds a single item. Multi-review walls are 3rd-party widgets (BlooTrue, Elfsight) on top of Fusion.
apps.notes: Fusion's 3-review-excerpt cap is a real product constraint — you literally cannot show full reviews or more than a few. Build only if a vertical (restaurants/bars) demands it; otherwise lead with Google reviews which most operators care about more.

apps.name: Tripadvisor
apps.howEmbedded2026: Official FREE widget exists (tripadvisor.com/Widgets) — enter business name, pick a fixed preset, copy a snippet. Keyless but rigid: fixed styling, no star-rating filtering, TA-branded. Deeper/customized use = the paid Content API or a 3rd-party widget (Smash Balloon, Endorsal, Embeddable).
apps.notes: Best of the three review sources for a quick keyless win: official widget, paste into WEBPAGE, done. Perfect for HOSPITALITY/RESTAURANT verticals. Accept the fixed TA styling or upsell the Content-API/3rd-party path later.

apps.name: Social Wall (aggregator-backed, multi-source)
apps.howEmbedded2026: The pragmatic answer to all the dead native embeds. A paid aggregator (Walls.io, EmbedSocial, Curator.io, Taggbox, Juicer, Flockler) handles the OAuth/business-account/token mess once, moderates content, and gives back ONE embeddable URL/iframe that mixes IG + FB + X + TikTok + LinkedIn + more. This is exactly what OptiSigns (Social Mix, Walls.io app) and Yodeck do. Pricing ~$19–$99/mo (Taggbox/EmbedSocial/Juicer) up to $250/30-day events (Walls.io); Walls.io has no free tier; Curator/Juicer have limited free tiers.
apps.notes: STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATION: make this the headline 'Social Wall' app. Two models — (a) operator pastes their own aggregator's published-wall URL into WEBPAGE (zero ToS risk to us, they pay the aggregator), or (b) VenueOS holds an aggregator API account and resells walls as a billed line item (Tier-3 managed model, matches our economic plan). Either way the aggregator absorbs the takedown/ToS/rate-limit liability that direct scraping would dump on us.

uxNotes: OptiSigns is the design benchmark: per-platform apps (Instagram, Facebook, X, etc.) PLUS a 'Social Mix' meta-app that blends IG+FB+X into one wall, PLUS a dedicated Walls.io app. Each social app offers multiple display MODES — Single Post, Social Wall, Social Kiosk, Bricks/masonry — with light/dark theme, background color, and scroll-speed controls. The mode picker is the key UX idea: the same source renders as a hero single-post OR a scrolling wall.

Yodeck's flow for the hard platforms is an explicit OAuth gate: 'Add app → name it → Login with Instagram → authorize Business/Creator account'. It tells the user up-front that personal accounts won't work. That honesty is the right model — our picker should label IG/FB/X/LinkedIn apps as 'Requires a business account login' before they click.

Vendors universally separate VIDEO platforms (YouTube/Vimeo/Twitch — instant, paste-URL, no login) from SOCIAL feeds (IG/FB/X — login or aggregator). Mirror that split in our library with two visual tiers so operators set expectations: 'Instant' apps vs 'Connect account' apps.

Aggregator apps are presented as first-class tiles (OptiSigns lists Walls.io as its own app). The operator builds the wall in the aggregator's UI, then pastes ONE URL. Our 'Add via URL' WEBPAGE path already supports this — the app layer just needs a branded wrapper + instructions.

Refresh cadence is surfaced as a setting because rate limits force it (Yodeck defaults Facebook to a 10-minute refresh). Our config form should expose a refresh interval per social app and default it conservatively so we don't trip Meta/X rate limits.

Every reviews widget enforces source attribution (Google/Yelp/Tripadvisor branding) — it's a ToS requirement, not optional. Bake the attribution into the widget chrome so operators can't accidentally violate terms.

The best pickers show a confidence/'we found it' badge and a one-line plain-English blurb per app — directly aligned with our Integration Concierge vision (paste your site → we suggest the social apps you already have).
doBetterIdeas: Lead with HONESTY in the picker, which competitors bury: tag each app 'Instant (no login)', 'Needs business-account login', or 'Powered by aggregator (subscription)'. Operators hate discovering mid-setup that their personal IG won't work — surfacing it builds trust and differentiates from OptiSigns/Yodeck's optimistic framing.

Tier the library by friction, not alphabetically: a top row of 'Instant' apps that ride our existing widgets with ZERO backend (YouTube, Vimeo, Pinterest, Tripadvisor, Bluesky, single-post X/TikTok/Snapchat) — we can ship these THIS sprint with just config forms over STREAMING/WEBPAGE. Then a 'Connect' row (IG/FB/Threads/LinkedIn) and an 'aggregator' row.

Let the Integration Concierge auto-detect social handles from the operator's pasted homepage (og:tags, footer social links) and pre-fill the app config — 'We found @yourvenue on Instagram and a 4.6-star Google profile; want them on screen?' Nobody else closes the loop from website-scrape → seeded social app.

Offer a VenueOS-managed aggregator tier (our Tier-3 managed-AI model applied to social): we hold one Walls.io/EmbedSocial enterprise account, the operator never sees an API key or a Meta app-review queue, and we bill it as a line item. This turns the single biggest pain (Meta App Review + business-account OAuth) into a one-click VenueOS-handles-it experience — the exact 'they don't need an IT consultant' wedge.

Build ONE Meta app review covering Instagram Graph + oEmbed Read + Threads, so all three Meta apps light up from a single OAuth. Amortize the weeks of app-review pain once across the whole Meta family instead of per-platform.

Provide signage-native display modes the social networks don't: full-bleed portrait single-post (for portrait LED), QR-to-follow overlay auto-generated from the handle, and an emergency-aware mode that auto-pauses the social wall when an emergency override fires (our unique safety moat — a social feed should never sit next to a lockdown alert).

Cache aggressively and degrade gracefully on the player: pre-render the latest N social items server-side into our Supabase bucket so a Taurus Chromium-83 kiosk or an offline player shows the last-known wall instead of a broken iframe — most signage rivals just show a white box when the embed script fails on old WebViews.

Default refresh intervals to rate-limit-safe values automatically per platform (e.g., FB 10 min, X conservative) and warn before an operator sets something that would trip a ban — turn the rate-limit footgun into an invisible guardrail.
